page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a high-capacity, memory-optimized instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Built on dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration bundles 512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation ratio, along with 3840 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU package incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16) alongside cryptographic hardware support for AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark assessments show top-tier processing power and memory throughput across multiple synthetic tests. The server records top 10% bracket scores in Geekbench multi-core (28,247) and Clang software compilation (63,809), backed by PassMark CPU scores of 98,751.74. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 533.09 GB/sec, while write operations reach 205.9 GB/sec. Data processing performance remains elevated with PassMark database operations ranking in the top 10% and Redis throughput reaching 111.85 million SET operations per second.

The bundled 3840 GB NVMe storage provides fast local I/O without relying on detached network block volumes, optimizing latency-sensitive data operations. While lacking dedicated hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs, the system demonstrates strong CPU-based inference capability, delivering 76.47 tokens per second during medium-model text generation. With substantial memory density and dedicated core reservations, the instance provides high compute density, though workloads that do not leverage the large 512 GB memory pool may see lower resource utilization relative to its scale.

This server profile fits heavy transactional and in-memory database engines, large Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehouse extraction, distributed build pipelines, and enterprise-grade web applications requiring massive cache space and fast local solid-state storage.
description: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a high-density, memory-optimized virtual server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 512 GB of RAM, offering 8 GB of memory per core, paired directly with 3840 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage. Architectural highlights include AVX-512 instruction support, 32 MB of L3 cache, and strong cryptographic acceleration. Synthetic testing places this instance in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core performance, PassMark database operations, and software compilation throughput, supplemented by uncached memory read bandwidth of 533.09 GB/sec. The absence of a discrete GPU limits graphical acceleration, but the combination of heavy CPU threading, high memory capacity, and expansive local flash storage makes it effective for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics platforms, distributed microservice backends, and high-throughput compilation clusters.
